title: Discovery of the ozone hole
summary: British Antarctic Survey scientists Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin published a paper in Nature on 16 May 1985 showing a steady springtime loss of ozone over Antarctica, measured at Halley. By 1984 the ozone layer there was only about two-thirds as thick as in earlier decades. The finding spurred international action on CFCs.

uncertainty.note: Date is the publication of the Nature paper; the measurements span the late 1970s to 1984.

as_recorded.value: published in a seminal Nature paper in May 1985

where.modern_name: Halley Research Station, Brunt Ice Shelf, Antarctica
where.historical_name: Halley Bay station (British Antarctic Survey), Brunt Ice Shelf, Antarctica

importance.justification: Revealed human-made ozone depletion and led to the Montreal Protocol.

beats.caption: Data from Halley show the ozone layer there only about two-thirds as thick as in earlier decades.
Farman, Gardiner and Shanklin publish the Halley record in Nature, reporting a yearly springtime drop.
The Montreal Protocol aims to freeze production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances at then-current rates.
